listitem.para: Whether ipsec add --autoall (run when &pluto; starts and whenever ipsec.conf is reloaded) should reconcile the running connection table against the configuration rather than only adding to it. When enabled, connections whose definition is unchanged are left in place (preserving their established SAs instead of being torn down and rebuilt), and connections that no longer appear in the configuration are swept away. When disabled, --autoall is additive only: removed connections linger and unchanged connections are re-added on every reload.

An address is only worked out when the connection is added when it is given as a DNS name, as %defaultroute, or as an interface name such as %ppp0, for left=, right=, leftnexthop= or rightnexthop=. &pluto; does not update such an address once it has been resolved, so these are re-resolved at the start of every --autoall. A connection is then left in place only when the addresses still resolve to what it is using. Otherwise, it is rebuilt to pick up the new address. A lookup that fails counts as a change, so the connection is rebuilt and the usual retry applies. Reloading therefore continues to pick up a peer or a default route that has moved.
